newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil re-election moves put back until Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: Brazil re-election moves put back until Oct 29.

text.p: A proposal that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the chance of a second term will only begin discussions in Congress on October 29, an aide to the government's leader in the lower house said.

A spokeswoman for Dep. Benito Gama said the first meeting of a committee to discuss, and eventually vote on, a constitutional amendment allowing re-election had been put back to give the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB) time to decide its position.

The government had hoped to kick off the discussions this week, but the PPB, one of the four biggest parties in the Chamber of Deputies, wants to consult party delegates before naming its members. That process is expected to take until the weekend.

The PPB is reported to want to remain out of the re-election debate until the second round of voting in municipal elections on November 15 when the party is is expected to win the mayoral race in Sao Paulo, Brazil's biggest city.

The PPB is considered decisive to the fate of the re-election bill in the Chamber of Deputies, because it controls around 90 of a total 513 deputies and because one of its leading members, Paulo Maluf, has said he may run for the presidency in 1998.
